newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada, India expand air and diplomatic ties.
newsitem.headline: Canada, India expand air and diplomatic ties.

text.p: Canada announced on Monday that it would expand air links with India and set up a new Canadian government office in India.

Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said that Air Canada and Air India would be allowed to increase by 30 percent the number of seats currently available for service between Canada and India, via Europe as before.
Axworthy made the announcement at a news conference with his Indian counterpart I.K. Gujral.

In addition, western-Canada-based Canadian Airlines International will be allowed to offer two weekly flights over the Pacific, and Air India will be able to add Amsterdam as an intermediate point between India and Canada.
Canada also plans to open a liaison office in Chandigarh, capital of India's Punjab State in January, to facilitate trade, investment and immigration and visitor visas.
Earlier in the day, Gujral visited Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, who led a trade mission to India in January.
